basis: The printing heads this block 'VERS. 10-18.' and it opens 'VERS. 10-18.-- Clauseruntque ostium viri, et eos qui erant foris percusserunt caecitate,'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Angelomus was a monk of Luxeuil in the middle of the ninth century and wrote for the Emperor Lothar I, who reigned from 840 to 855 and whom the verse prooemium addresses. The Genesis commentary is placed with his commentaries on Kings and on the Song of Songs in that decade. The wiki header gives the eleventh century, which is a century and a half out and is not followed. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1852 printing.
text:
VERS. 10-18.-- Clauseruntque ostium viri, et eos qui erant foris percusserunt caecitate, etc.

Graeci habent, aorosia [aorasia], quod magis dici potest, avidentia, quae faciat non videre, non omnia, sed quod opus non est. Hac enim aorosia et illi percussi sunt, qui quaerebant Eliseum. Moraliter vero, quid est quod, malis adversantibus, intra domum | Lot reducitur et munitur, nisi quod justus quisque, dum pravorum insidias sustinet, ad mentem revertitur et imperterritus manet? Sodomitae autem viri in domo Lot invenire ostium nequeunt, quia corruptores mentium contra vitam justi nullum accusationis aditum deprehendunt. Percussi enim caecitate quasi domum circumeunt, qui invidentes facta dictaque perscrutantur. Sed quia eis de vita justi fortis undique ac laudabilis actio obviat, errantes nil aliud quam parietem palpant.
